column1: # Annotation queue for #111 Part B. ONE PAPER PER SESSION.
# Open a fresh session and give it:
# Ordered by DISAGREEMENT, easiest first: `score` is the count of entity
# names present in one arm and not the other, plus twice the run-count
# difference. Low score means the arms mostly agree, so those papers are
# quick and they calibrate your judgement before the hard ones.
# runs_A / runs_B are the two arms' run counts -- they match on only 5 of
# 26 papers, so expect to adjudicate runs on nearly every paper.
# NOTE rows 10 and 26: both arms returned ZERO runs. Row 10 is a position
# paper and row 26 a survey, so `runs: []` is probably correct -- these are
# the reference cases for 'the paper ran nothing'. Row 26 still carries the
# largest entity disagreement in the set (79), because a survey names
# everything; consider it last or skip it if 10-20 papers is the budget.
# The owner wants 10-20 of these 26. Taking them in order gives the
# cheapest 10-20 and leaves the tedious tail unspent.
